coverage.summary: Residential dwellings and units statewide, including units in mobilehome parks. Exempt: housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (rolling, except mobilehomes), deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing, school and university dormitories, housing under a stricter local rent or price control, qualifying separately alienable property with the written notice, and owner-occupied duplexes with no ADU/JADU. Homeowners of mobilehomes are not covered.
coverage.owner_conditions: The separately-alienable exemption applies only if the owner is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management, and the written exemption notice was given (in the rental agreement for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after July 1, 2020, or July 1, 2022 for mobilehomes). The owner-occupied duplex exemption lasts only while the owner continues in occupancy.
coverage.other_conditions: Under subd. (d)(3), housing subject to local rent or price control consistent with Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.) that limits annual increases below this cap is exempt, so the stricter local control applies instead. The section does not expand or limit local authority under ch. 2.7.

result.notes: I removed the example cities (Los Angeles, San Francisco, Berkeley, Santa Ana) from other_conditions. No supplied document names them. D040, the LAHD page cited in also_supported_by, is not among the supplied documents, so it was not used. I set new_construction_exemption.requires_owner_filing to null. Subd. (d)(4) suggests the exemption is automatic, but no passage states that no filing is required. min_building_age_years=15 is derived from the rolling 15-year certificate-of-occupancy exemption: coverage turns on the certificate's age, not the building's age. construction_cutoff stays null because the exemption is rolling, not a fixed date. All other values are supported by D024 (Civ. Code § 1947.12).
